title: A day on board a dahabiya
standfirst: What a dahabiya day actually looks like, from the first coffee on deck to dinner at a quiet mooring. For the boat itself, see our page on the [[up]].

sections.heading: Morning
paragraphs: Days start early, before the heat. Breakfast is on the upper deck as the crew make ready to sail. On many mornings there is a short visit ashore first: a temple, a village or a quarry that the larger ships don’t stop at.

sections.heading: Sailing
paragraphs: Most of the day is spent on the water. The sails go up when there is wind, and the boat moves at walking pace past fields, palm groves and fishing boats. Lunch is usually served on board while sailing.

sections.heading: Afternoon and evening
paragraphs: In the late afternoon the dahabiya moors at a riverbank or an island. There is time for a walk or a swim from the shore where it is safe, then dinner on deck. With no other ships alongside, the evenings are dark and quiet.

faqs.q: Is there anything to do on board?
faqs.a: The main pleasures are the river, the deck and the company. There are no shows or casinos; some dahabiyas have a small library.
Full board is usual on a dahabiya. Each cruise’s page lists what is included.

seoTitle: A day on board a dahabiya on the Nile
seoDescription: From breakfast on deck to a quiet mooring at night: what a typical day on a Nile dahabiya cruise is like.
